title: Choir and Well
premise: Yara Blackwood, a property surveyor, is sent to appraise Hollowmere House, a decaying estate whose previous owners vanished mid-census. The house keeps its own ledger: every night, a well in the cellar counts the living under its roof, and when the count reaches the number it wants by the harvest moon, the house 'harvests' — taking voices, memories, and finally bodies. Yara's sleep recordings reveal a second voice answering questions he never asked aloud, and his estranged half-brother Theo arrives uninvited, pulled to the house by dreams of their dead mother. To survive, Yara must forge a found family from strangers trapped inside, teach them to lie to the count, and ultimately offer the house a memory in place of a life — ending with Yara walking out alive but unable to remember why the others are crying at the gate.
about_author: Ulyana Eriksen is a former building inspector who spent a decade cataloguing condemned properties across the northern coast before turning her case files into fiction. She writes horror about structures that remember, and lives in a house she refuses to have surveyed.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He arrives at Hollowmere House for a routine survey and finds rooms that measure differently on every pass, plus a cellar well that echoes back sounds no one made. The emotional beat is professional denial curdling into unease as he signs the intake ledger and feels the pen move slightly without him.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, interwoven with flashbacks. He sets up sleep-recording equipment, telling himself the tapping is pipes, the humming is wind. A flashback shows his childhood home and the first voice he explained away. The beat is the comfort of rationality beginning to crack; the recorder's red light stays on all night like an eye.

chapters.title: Playback
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The recording captures him asleep — and a second voice answering questions he never asked, reciting names, dates, and one name that stops his heart: his mother's. The beat is dread and grief colliding; he realizes the house has been interviewing him in his sleep.

chapters.title: Theo at the Gate
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Theo arrives uninvited, drawn by dreams of their dead mother standing at this exact gate. The siblings' reunion is prickly, full of fifteen years of silence. The beat is wary tenderness — and horror when Theo describes the house perfectly despite never seeing photos.

chapters.title: The Others
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Three squatters are already living there: Marisol, a nurse; Dev, a teenage runaway; and old Petey, who has survived here longest because he never sleeps. They explain the rule obliquely: don't answer anything after dark. The beat is reluctant community forming around shared fear.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The well begins counting aloud each midnight — five voices, though six people live in the house. Someone is being counted twice, or something extra is counted among them. Paranoia fractures the group. The beat is suspicion replacing solidarity as everyone audits everyone.

chapters.title: What the Well Wants
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Researching the estate, she finds the pattern: every harvest moon, the house reaches its quota and takes. Petey confesses he gave it his wife's memory decades ago to stay alive. The beat is terrible clarity — survival has always had a price, and someone has been paying it.

chapters.title: Lies After Dark
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The group trains itself to answer the house falsely, feeding it wrong names and invented memories to corrupt the count. It works — until the house starts asking about things only the dead would know, using their mother's voice. The beat is desperate ingenuity shadowed by intimate violation.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: Full ensemble POV, rapid cuts. The moon rises, the count climbs, and the house takes Dev's voice mid-scream. Yara realizes the quota can be met another way: a whole life's worth of memory, freely given. Climax beat — sacrifice chosen over loss, family forged in the cellar's cold breath.

chapters.title: Six at the Gate
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Dawn. Five people walk out of Hollowmere House; Yara walks out too, but empty — he traded his memories of them all. At the gate, the four survivors weep over a stranger who politely asks who they are. Final beat: found family persists even when only one side remembers finding it.
